title: Longitudinal sonographic measurement of the pylorus in preterm infants ≤ 30 0/7 weeks’ gestation
summary:
Background: At the junction between the stomach and the small intestine lies a ring-shaped muscle known as the pylorus. It controls the rate at which the stomach’s contents are passed on. In infants, this muscle can thicken and narrow the exit from the stomach. This can be detected using ultrasound, a painless examination that involves no radiation. In order to interpret the measurements correctly, reference values from healthy children of the same age are required. For preterm babies, whose pylorus is still developing, such reference values have so far been virtually non-existent.

Research question: We wish to determine the thickness of the muscle layer and the diameter of the pylorus in preterm babies, and how these values change over the course of the first few weeks of life. This will enable us to establish reference values for preterm infants.

Methodology: The study will include preterm infants born at ≤ 30 0/7 weeks’ gestation who are being cared for on our ward, provided their parents give their consent. The pylorus is measured by ultrasound in each child at four specified time points. The examination takes only a short time, is painless and is carried out as part of routine bedside care. No treatments are altered and no additional procedures are performed. The measurements are analysed collectively and published in a scientific journal.

interventions.name:
Longitudinal characterisation of pyloric muscle thickness (PMT)  and pyloric diameter (PD) in preterm infants ≤30 0/7 weeks’ gestation at defined
postmenstrual ages (30 0/7, 32 0/7, 34 0/7, 36 0/7 weeks’ gestation
(wge)).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy preterm infants ≤30 0/7 weeks’ gestation. Written parental consent has been obtained
Exclusion criteria:
Congenital gastrointestinal malformations (including pyloric stenosis, intestinal atresia,
gastroschisis, omphalocele). Chromosomal abnormalities. Lack of parental consent.
